claim: MQTT last-will messages fire only on ungraceful client disconnects; a graceful HA (or agent) shutdown does NOT trigger the LWT, so the status topic stays stale 'online'.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent needs a SIGTERM handler publishing offline (shutdown message) because systemd stops are graceful and LWT will not fire
scope_conditions: HA MQTT client, mosquitto-class brokers, 2018-2020 era but MQTT-spec-inherent
quoted_support: Update 2: Looks like will_message is only sent on ungraceful mqtt client disconnect. Since restarting hass is likely a graceful shutdown, no message is sent.

claim: The birth message published on every HA start is the standard trigger for devices (e.g. zigbee2mqtt) to republish their cached state, i.e. birth-message-driven state resync is the ecosystem convention.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent should subscribe to HA's birth topic and republish current state + discovery on HA restart
quoted_support: I do see birth_message publishing every time when hassio is started which then triggers zigbee2mqtt to repulish its cached state. So the end result is its working for what I needed.

claim: With the UI-configured MQTT integration, HA's own client birth/will can only be configured by editing .storage/core.config_entries while HA is stopped — a fragile, officially unsupported workaround.
stance_target: fleet design should not depend on HA-side birth/will config; per-device (agent-side) availability is the robust path
quoted_support: if you stop HA, you can edit the .storage/core.config_entries ... Home assistant must be stopped otherwise it will overwrite your changes. If you mess anything up, HA will refuse to start

claim: HA shutdown-trigger automations publishing an offline MQTT message are 'hit or miss' because the shutdown event may not complete before process exit.
stance_target: agent-side graceful-shutdown publishing (in-process, before disconnect) is more reliable than HA-side shutdown automations
quoted_support: The only recommendation is to use an automation with an home assistant trigger for shutdown, but that tends to be hit or miss.

claim: Birth and last will are functions of the MQTT client, not the broker — each connecting client registers its own LWT at CONNECT time.
stance_target: ha-linux-agent (the client) owns its own availability contract; the broker merely stores and fires it
quoted_support: Birth and last will are a function of the mqtt client not the broker.
